{{Short description|Japanese mathematician}}

'''Yukio Matsumoto''' ({{Lang|ja|松本 幸夫}}, ''Matsumoto Yukio''; born 1944) is a Japanese mathematician, who worked mostly in the field of [[geometric topology]] and [[low-dimensional topology]]. He was a former professor for mathematics at the [[University of Tokyo]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=https://researchmap.jp/read0007856?lang=en |title=Yukio Matsumoto |website=researchmap.jp |publisher=researchmap |access-date=2022-11-08 }}</ref>

He received his Ph.D. in 1973 from the [[university of Tokyo]] and his supervisor was [[Ichiro Tamura]].<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=98278}}</ref>

In 1984, he won the [[Iyanaga Prize]] of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]].<ref name="auto" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/en/list/winners-list.html|title=List of Spring and Autumn Prizes Winners|website=www.mathsoc.jp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Introduction to Gakushuin University – Overview of the Faculty of Science |url=https://www.gakushuin.ac.jp/univ/new/pamphlet-english.pdf |page=11}}</ref>
